title: Premier Excluded Total: Itemization Schedule
content:
**GAP Waiver Addenda: Premier exclusion schedule for GAP Waiver Premier 150 claims.**

**The claim.** The claim is the latest claim reported on the addendum: the claim with the latest reporting date, or, where two claims were reported on that date, the one recorded first on the addendum.

**The total.** The Premier excluded total is the sum of six parts, added without rounding and then rounded half-up to the cent: the past-due part, the fee part, the deferral part, the placed-premium part, the add-on part and the uncovered-deductible part.

| Part | Amount |
|---|---|
| Past-due part | the installments it counts, which are all the installments treated as past due, times the installment amount it uses, which is the contract's scheduled payment, less the partial installment credit the contract carries, never below 0.00 |
| Fee part | the fees due the contract carries less the late charges assessed on installments that fell due after the date of loss, never below 0.00 |
| Deferral part | the deferred installments it counts, which are all the installments deferred by every extension the contract records, times the installment amount it uses, which is the contract's scheduled payment |
| Placed-premium part | every force-placed premium the insurance tracking record added to the contract balance |
| Add-on part | the price of the service contract financed on the contract times the calendar days from the date of loss to its expiration date, divided by the calendar days from its enrollment date to its expiration date, rounded half-up to the cent, when it was enrolled on or before the date of loss and expires after it; 0.00 when there is no such service contract |
| Uncovered-deductible part | the primary deductible the claim shows less the deductible covered the claim shows, never below 0.00 |

**Installments treated as past due.** These are the installments still unpaid that fell due on or before the date of loss. They are counted from the contract's next due date, one a month, through the date of loss: the whole months from the next due date to the date of loss, plus one. None are counted when the next due date is after the date of loss.

**Whole months.** Whole months from one date to a later one are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

**Installments that fell due after the date of loss.** For the fee part, these are the installments whose due date is fewer whole months before today than a set figure. That figure is the whole months from the contract's next due date to today, less the whole months from the next due date to the date of loss.

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

| Part | Hypothetical records | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Past-due | 2 installments treated as past due, scheduled payment 410.00, partial installment credit 55.00 | 765.00 |
| Fee | fees due 120.00, of which late charges on installments due after the loss are 30.00 | 90.00 |
| Deferral | 2 installments deferred by extensions, scheduled payment 410.00 | 820.00 |
| Placed-premium | premiums added to the contract balance | 288.00 |
| Add-on | service contract price 1500.00, 400 of its 1095 days remaining after the loss | 547.95 |
| Uncovered-deductible | primary deductible 800.00, deductible covered 350.00 | 450.00 |
| **Premier excluded total** | | **2960.95** |
